facts.value: Architecture is the study and practice of designing structures, especially habitable ones. It utilizes civil engineering techniques but is considered a visual art. It is both the process and the product of sketching, conceiving, planning, designing, and constructing buildings or other structures.

The practice of architecture has been used as a way of expressing culture by civilizations worldwide since the prehistoric era. Architectural works are perceived as cultural symbols and as works of art.

Texts on architecture have been written since ancient times. The earliest surviving text is the 1st century BC treatise 'De architectura' by Vitruvius. Concepts defining good buildings include durability, utility, and beauty, advancing through historical figures like Leon Battista Alberti and Louis Sullivan.
The idea of sustainable architecture was introduced in the late 20th century.

Modern architecture began after World War I as an avant-garde movement focused on a new style for a new social and economic order, emphasizing modern techniques, materials, and simplified geometric forms.
